jobs.title: Senior Director, Operations Finance
jobs.description:
Job Summary:


**WHO ARE WE?**

Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media \& Sponsorship. Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 620 million tickets sold annually and approximately 10,000 clients worldwide. Live Nation Concerts is the largest provider of live entertainment in the world promoting more than 50,000 events annually for nearly 7,000 artists in 40\+ countries. These businesses allow Live Nation Media \& Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com .  



**WHO ARE YOU?**

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on!  



**THE ROLE**

Reporting to the Vice President, Operations Finance, the Senior Director, Operations Finance owns operational accounting for Live Nation Canada. This is the senior operating leader of a function that accounts for every show, venue and festival we run in this country; tens of thousands of transactions a year, settled under contract in a fast\-paced environment where the work is visible and the stakes are real.  



  

The Senior Director’s mission will be to elevate the function by building a high\-performing team and setting standards nationally for how shows and venues are accounted for. They will be responsible to evolve current processes toward greater automation, control and scale. Success in the first 12 months will be clear and measurable: a functioning management layer that consistently delivers on deadlines; a faster, cleaner close with a defensible timetable and fewer post\-close adjustments; one written national process standard in use across all markets; an automated end\-to\-end workflow that is live, adopted and measurably reducing manual effort or error; and a strong control environment where audit findings are closed promptly and none repeat. Working in close partnership with the Vice President, the Senior Director will help shape the direction and priorities of the function. They will be the trusted go\-to partner for the business on all matters of operational accounting.  



  

This is a great opportunity to own a national function, build a team around it, and elevate how Live Nation Canada does its accounting.  



  

**WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO**

**Leadership**

* Own the structure, capability and performance of a \~12\-person operational accounting team spanning show settlement, venue accounting and financial close
* Lead through managers: develop the management layer, set clear ownership accountabilities, establish performance standards and hold managers accountable for their teams' deadlines and quality
Own talent strategy for the function: hiring standards, onboarding, development plans, succession depth, and a coverage model that holds through peak season, festival periods and major tours  
* 

  

**Event Reporting and Operational Accounting**

* Accountable for the completeness, accuracy and timeliness of all events, venues and festivals accounting nationally (including the integrity of reported contribution margin by show, venue and market)
* Own the close calendar end to end and commit to the timetable; ensure corporate reporting deadlines are consistently met
* Own the accounting treatment of show settlement: from artist final settlements against contract, withholding tax, charity and merchandise/bundle recognition, co\-promoted events, joint venture splits, venue expense settlement and shared ancillary revenue
* Own accounting for owned and operated venues, including inventory, labour costs and cash handling
* Own balance sheet integrity for the function: reconciliation quality, accrual adequacy, deferred revenue, AR aging and collections performance for event\-related balances
* Develop and recommend accounting positions on complex deal structures such as co\-promoted events, joint ventures, festival vehicles, rental versus promoted, international artist withholding, multi\-year ancillary agreements
* Partner with regional controllers to ensure consistent application of policy across markets, and resolve differences rather than reporting them
* Partner with VP, Operational Accounting and Corporate for all technical accounting approval
* Accountable for the day\-to\-day operation of internal controls over settlement, cash floats, AP approval and wire release, including SOX\-relevant controls in scope
* Play a critical role in internal and external audits; owning remediation of findings to closure while ensuring every settlement is audit\-ready with proper documentation backup
Proactively identify control gaps as volume, venues and deal structures change, and implement corrective action  
* 

  

**National Responsibilities**

* Develop, implement and sustain a national operational accounting playbook: settlement process, documentation standards, close process and checklist, reconciliation methodology, escalation path.
* Identify and improve workstreams end to end; from business case through delivery to adoption and measured benefit
* Define and report the function's operating metrics: days to close, settlement cycle time, restatement and error rates, aged AR, control exception volume. Use them to drive decisions and continuous improvement
Own the data standards that allow event economics to be reported consistently  
* 

  

**Partner with the business**

* Provide the actuals, trend data and event\-level insight that Strategic Finance and FP\&A build the budget and forecast on; accountable for the reliability of what they plan from
* Support due diligence, integration planning and

jobs.title: Director, Information Systems
jobs.description:
The Director/Senior Director Technology Audit and Advisory Services is accountable for the delivery of high quality, professional, cost\-effective, value\-added, and risk\-based internal audit services over Technology functions, across North America (Canada and US Segment), Global Wealth \& Asset Management, Group Functions, and the Global Data Technology Office. The role reports to the AVP of North America Segment Technology, Audit Services.

  

  

**Position Responsibilities:**


* Audit Delivery – Delivery of North America Segment Technology, Infrastructure and Cybersecurity (steady state/key risk, program and project, business integrated, issue assessments).
* Technology SOX – Delivery of application and infrastructure technology SOX audit work and to drive our approach and processes for this work forward through use of automation, data analytics, and shared services.
* Reporting and Planning – Execution and continuous improvement of reporting processes in support of the larger technology audit organization, as well as annual audit planning, resource management, and other process improvements for the immediate North America segment technology audit team.
* Other – Audit initiatives, engagements, and process improvements as assigned.
  

  

**Strategic Leadership**


* Understand the company’s strategy, operations, and regulatory environment to proactively identify areas of emerging and heightened risk related to technology that affects the company
* Support the development of an audit strategy that aligns to business, technology, and Audit Services strategies, provides sufficient coverage for key risks while meeting regulatory expectations
* Develop internal procedures and tools to drive consistency across all engagements and drive audit planning
* Help improve Technology SOX delivery and quality to improve efficiencies through increased use of data analytics, automation and shared services and other innovations
* Develop and produce meaningful reports for Senior Technology Management that identify trends and enable continuous improvement of risks and controls
* Contribute to the development of Audit Services procedures, strategy, and direction; continually improve audit and supporting processes leveraging technology to the fullest
  

  

**Audit Delivery and Oversight**


* Plan and direct audits and special audit projects to objectively evaluate the effectiveness of key controls and adequacy of risk management practices; collaborating with management to obtain a consensus on establishing the problem, risks exposure; produce meaningful audit reports that clearly articulate the position on risks and related issues, while meeting Audit Services operational targets related to budget, timeline and quality of execution
* Delivery of annual Technology Application and Infrastructure ITGC SOX work, in collaboration with Technology Management, SOX PMO, and external audit
* Perform integrated/cross\-functional audits in partnership with groups across Audit Services to provide comprehensive reporting on risks that could prevent the achievement of Management’s objectives
* Support the development of an annual audit plan using risk management processes, in collaboration with Management and Audit Services leadership
* Drive innovation and incorporate and develop industry best practices into forward thinking audit approach; manage Audit Services’ resources efficiently, economically, and effectively
* Provide management with timely recommendations that reduce risk, help them run their business better, make strategic and operational decisions, and oversee management of risks and controls
* Monitoring progress in implementing control recommendations and reporting thereon; assist with preparation of Audit Committee and senior leadership reports

  

**Leadership \& People Development**


* Lead and develop a high\-caliber audit team, attract, and retain top talent and provide appropriate development, coaching and training
* Foster creative culture that strives for continuous improvement and welcomes and offers feedback—enabling best\-in\-class audit practices
* Challenge, coach and enable the team members to develop to their fullest and maximize their contribution to the team
* Drive team skills development and engagement; manage talent across the team for development and succession and rotate change expertise

  

**Stakeholder Management**


* Managing Management’s expectations regarding assurance and advisory work deadlines and deliverables
* Providing relevant stakeholders with an overview of audit work and commentary on the control environment, including trends and emerging issues that could impact the Company
* Collaborate effectively with divisional and global stakeholders in Technology and Information Risk Management
* Establishing a high level of credibility and building professional relationships with key stakeholders responsible for technology and information risk across the Company

  

**Required Qualifications:**


* Exceptional communications judgement and the ability to communicate clearly and succinctly to effectively deliver key messages verbally and in writing and to listen and consider various perspectives; confident presentation and facilitation skills and strong interpersonal and leadership skills to facilitate working with senior management at all levels
* Ability to quickly understand business processes and risks, identify key controls, analyze complex situations, reach appropriate conclusions, make value\-added and practical recommendations and influence management to take appropriate actions on recommendations
* In\-depth knowledge of audit methodologies, project management and system development methodologies (including Agile), control frameworks and risk management practices, and regulatory requirements; Exceptional understanding of how technology supports business strategies, the latest technology and cyber security trends, best practices, and industry standards; excel

jobs.title: Director, Corporate Client Group Finance
jobs.description:
**Job Description**

**What is the opportunity?**

  

As Director, Corporate Client Group Finance (CCGF), you are part of the mid\-market Corporate Banking team and play a key role in the realization of Corporate Client Group (CCG) objectives through the structuring, delivery and management of the bank debt of a targeted customer base. We target loan origination in the Canadian mid\-market, including large Canadian subsidiaries of foreign multinationals, private and small cap public Canadian companies, and are responsible for meeting annually established targets for loan derived revenues and returns by providing advice to our partners on optimizing the use of lending in connection with broader RBC relationship goals.

 **What will you do?**

* Support CCG relationship managers to structure, deliver, close, and monitor loan transactions under direction of the Senior Director CCG Finance, including credit submissions and transaction presentations
* Support CCG relationship managers in the preparation and presentation of marketing pitches to existing and potential clients
* Follow up and engage with RBC partners and functions including Group Risk Management, Private Banking, RBC Investments, Capital Markets, specialized teams in Commercial Financial Services (leasing, trade finance etc.), Personal Banking, and others
* Work with Group Risk Management to ensure proper alignment with credit processes and client expectations Provide research, analysis, and data (market, industry, client, and competitor) to support CCG advice on the optimal amount of bank debt required to meet strategic objectives with each client relationship
* Take part in the national team of CCG Finance underwriters committed to the delivery of quality credit products to RBC clients and targets
* Provide analysis and support to Senior Director CCG Finance and CCG Finance colleagues for advice on risk and return associated with loan transactions contemplated as part of client strategies

 **What do you need to succeed?**

 **Must\-have**

* Undergraduate degree in Business, Economics, Accounting, or Finance
* Strong quantitative, financial modeling, and analytical skills with an ability to analyze company financial statements
* Knowledge of credit, credit metrics, credit structuring and the capability to work through Loan Agreements and other legal documents
* Advanced skills with Excel, Word, PowerPoint and the ability to source data/research
* Professional oral and written communication skills with a high level of attention to detail in both written and financial work
* Ability to perform well under pressure, meet time sensitive deadlines, prioritize work and multi\-task responsibilities while working on multiple projects
* Well organized and able to set priorities and devote appropriate attention to each assignment

 **Nice\-to\-have**

* MBA, CPA or CFA
* Work experience in corporate lending/corporate finance
* Trained in credit and accounting with an ability to manage complex concepts

 **What’s in it for you?**

  

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

* Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
* Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high\-performing team
* Opportunities to do challenging work

**Primary Purpose**

  

The Senior Director, Information Technology (SDIT) leads the Faculty of Engineering’s information technology strategy and operations and is accountable for the overall results of Engineering IT. The role translates institutional priorities into innovative, reliable, and service\-oriented solutions that support excellence in teaching, learning, research, and administration


The SDIT provides strategic leadership and oversight for the Faculty's technology services, infrastructure, and innovation portfolio, including IT support services, enterprise infrastructure and application services, audiovisual and classroom technologies, and research computing. The role ensures technology services are responsive, scalable, and aligned with the Faculty's academic, research, and operational objectives, while fostering strong stakeholder partnerships, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across all technology functions.


Reporting directly to the Executive Officer, the SDIT provides strategic and operational leadership for information technology across the Faculty of Engineering. The SDIT is accountable for translating priorities into coordinated technology strategies, initiatives, and services that advance the Faculty’s mission and core values. As the information technology expert, the SDIT oversees all information technology functions and personnel, ensuring the delivery of reliable, secure, innovative, and client\-focused technology solutions. The role is responsible for establishing a service\-oriented culture grounded in continuous improvement, operational excellence, collaboration, and accountability while aligning technology investments and resources with the Faculty’s strategic objectives. The SDIT leads a diverse portfolio of IT professionals operating within an academic environment, providing direction for technology governance, infrastructure, enterprise applications, information security, research computing support, digital transformation initiatives, and user services. Through strong operational leadership and strategic partnership with academic and administrative leaders, the SDIT enables the Faculty to maintain and enhance its reputation as a world\-class leader in engineering education and research.  



  

The SDIT fosters effective partnerships with academic, administrative, and external stakeholders to advance the Faculty’s strategic objectives. The role is responsible for bringing critical issues, risks, opportunities, and emerging trends to the attention of leadership, providing informed strategic advice, and driving the evolution and execution of the Faculty’s information technology vision to support innovation, operational excellence, and long\-term institutional success. The SDIT also serves as Engineering’s senior IT liaison to the Chief Information Officer and IST, ensuring Faculty priorities are represented in institutional IT planning and that Engineering’s technology services align with University IT governance, standards and efficiency through shared services.

* Provides overall leadership for the Faculty’s information technology organizational structure, ensuring roles, responsibilities, reporting relationships, and service delivery models are clearly defined, strategically aligned, and well positioned to meet current and future business needs.
* Establishes a cohesive and integrated technology organization by bringing together distributed and centralized IT functions under a common vision, governance framework, service standards, and operating principles.
* Creates and aligns strategic, governance, standards\-setting, and operational activities across all Faculty information technology functions and personnel to ensure the consistent delivery of reliable, secure, scalable, and innovative technology services.
* Works with Engineering leadership and the Chief Information Officer to align the development and implementation of technology governance structures within Engineering to the institutional IT governance framework, including decision\-making processes, policies, and accountability frameworks that support effective prioritization, resource allocation, risk management, and operational excellence.

jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

**Position:** Director of Finance and Administration

**Location:** Martin Luther University College, Waterloo, Ontario

**Hours:** Full\-time, 35 hours per week, 8:30am to 4:30pm, In office at least 4 days a week

**Reports to:** Principal\-Dean

**Direct Reports:** 1 \- 2 roles

**Salary:** $90,000 \- $120,000 annually

**Start date**: December 2026

**This is an existing vacancy.**

**Position Summary**

Martin Luther University College (Luther) is a public university college federated with Wilfrid Laurier University. We are a faith\-based academic community committed to excellence in teaching, research, and community engagement.

The Director of Finance and Administration provides strategic and operational leadership for Luther’s financial and administrative functions. Reporting to the Principal\-Dean, the Director is responsible for financial reporting, compliance, planning and budgeting, internal controls, and administrative systems that support the long\-term financial sustainability of the institution and its mission.

**Responsibilities**

**Leadership of Financial Planning, Management, and Reporting**

* Ensure all necessary financial operations (including the operating budget), reporting, cash management, expenditure controls and other controls are in place and operating effectively to support Luther’s operations and the Board’s fiduciary obligations.
* Prepare financial analysis and reports as needed including operating statements (revenues and expenditures), budget forecasts, and forecast of cash flow for use by the Principal\-Dean, responsible managers or faculty, and the Finance Committee to support informed decision\-making and organizational accountability for a $4 Million operating budget.
* Manage the allocation of annual realized gains from endowment funds and reconcile investment manager’s reports for endowed and non\-endowed investments, resolving discrepancies.
* Take the initiative to manage investment transactions required as part of the annual budget or operations. Coordinate the flow of investment deposits and investment income with investment manager. Liaise with Luther’s investment manager and/or Finance Committee on investment issues for accounting purposes.
* Prepare annual unaudited financial statements and all reconciliations, supporting schedules, background reporting, and year end entries and adjustments required for the annual audit; prepare an audit package and manage the annual audit with the external auditors once per year, including: Schedule the audit and associated activities, Negotiate the audit contract for recommendation to the Finance Committee, Manage Luther’s elements of the process, Ensure a clean audit.
* Assist Luther’s staff and faculty in understanding and using relevant financial information. Support them in budget development for their areas or projects.
* Understand in detail and make recommendations to enhance the funding agreements between Luther and Wilfrid Laurier University and be able to advise the Principal\-Dean on the implications to annual revenue of proposed revisions to these agreements.
* Maximize the use of accounting software reporting capabilities where possible.
* Manage the financial elements of grant projects, supporting the assigned project manager in planning and tracking financial commitments, and in financial reporting for the project.
* Prepare and submit annual financial and statistical reporting required by external organizations such as Canada Revenue Agency (Registered Charity Information Return \-\- T3010, HST), Council of Ontario Universities (detailed analytical financial report), Association of Theological Schools, and others as required. Consult with these organizations regarding reporting requirements as necessary.
* Develop the annual capital budget (including equipment) for Board approval to maintain the Luther’s physical assets and avoid undue deferred maintenance.
* Oversee the implementation of the capital budget.
* Manage the financial elements of capital and construction projects.
* Manage the financial elements of capital and construction projects.

**General Administration**

* Act as the Chief Compliance Officer for reporting and legal requirements.

**Policy Coordination and Board Support**

* Coordinate policy needs and improvements with the Principal\-Dean to ensure all operational and board policies are consistently organized, reviewed, updated, and in compliance.

**Support to the Principal\-Dean**

* Support the activities of the Principal\-Dean through research, high\-level project/program development and implementation, implementation of confidential activities and other areas as they arise from time to time.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field
* CPA designation
* A minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in finance or accounting
* A minimum of 3 years of leadership or management experience
* Ability to lead strategically while maintaining hands\-on responsibility for day\-to\-day financial and administrative operations in a lean organizational environment
* Ability to work effectively within a governance\-based environment, supporting boards and collaborating with diverse interest holders
* Experience in a post\-secondary institution, public sector, or medium non\-profit organization is preferred
* Strong knowledge of public sector and/or fund accounting
* Advanced financial planning, budgeting, and analytical skills
* Ability to communicate complete financial information clearly to non\-financial interest holders
* Strong leadership, collaboration and relationship\-management skills
* High level of integrity, judgment, and professional discretion
* Experience with enterprise resource planning and financial reporting systems
